title: Keyboard-Only Operation
description: Complete real tasks with no pointing device, and diagnose what breaks when you can't — tab order, focus visibility, keyboard traps, skip links and landmarks, and custom controls that silently drop keyboard support.

title: Screen Readers: Actually Using One
description: Navigate a page with a screen reader using the commands real users navigate with — getting NVDA or VoiceOver running, browse mode versus focus mode, quick-navigation by heading/landmark/link/form field, the rotor and elements list, and listening for updates that never get announced at all.

title: Semantics, Roles and the Accessibility Tree
description: Read the accessibility tree and explain why an element is announced the way it is — what the browser exposes and to whom, native elements versus div-with-a-click-handler, the name/role/value every control owes, ARIA that helps versus ARIA that overrides something correct, and inspecting the tree directly in devtools.

title: Magnification, Zoom and Low Vision
description: Review a product the way someone using 400% zoom or a magnifier actually experiences it — reflow and the horizontal scrollbar that shouldn't exist, text spacing overrides that shatter a layout, measuring contrast and the cases the ratio misses, context loss under a screen magnifier, and what breaks under forced-colours mode.

title: Switch Access and Voice Control
description: Review for input methods that are slow, imprecise, or entirely speech-driven — switch scanning and why every extra control costs real time, target size and motor precision, voice control's dependence on accessible names, timeouts that assume a fast user, and drag or hover interactions with no alternative.
